PullRequest.Title: Agents window: start a new session in a chat window
PullRequest.Body:

## What

In the Agents window, a chat window (`sessions.chatWindows.enabled`) can now start a new session in place. New Session in a chat window opens an empty new-session composer as a chat tab next to the window's active chat:

- **Entry points:**
  - **Agents: New Session** (F1);
  - Cmd/Ctrl+N while the chat window has focus (in a text editor of the window it still creates an untitled file);
  - New Session in the window's Sessions picker, with Alt+Enter / Cmd+Enter to open it beside the active chat.

  There is no title bar button. When the active chat is an unsent composer, New Session focuses it.
- **Defaults:** the composer starts from the active chat's session: its folder (or No Workspace), agent and provider, model, mode, and Dev Container environment. The new session joins that session's custom group in the sessions list. All of these can be changed before sending.
- **Send:** a foreground send turns the tab into the new session's main chat, in the same tab and with focus kept. The chat stays in this window, held out of the main window's grid like the window's other chats. The main window's composer and grid are untouched.
- **Background send (Send in Background, Alt+Enter by default):** the session starts in the background and shows in the sessions list, in its group. The composer stays as is, reseeded with the same target, and shows "Message sent" with Open Session. If the background send fails, the prompt goes back into the composer when nothing changed there; otherwise a notification offers Restore Prompt and Copy Prompt.
- **Restore:** unsent composers, with their input, come back with their window after a reload.
- **Moves:** until its session is sent, a composer can't leave its window. Move to Main Window is disabled while the window holds an unsent composer, and moving or copying the composer to another or a new window is refused, with the reason. Once sent, the chat moves like any other.
- **Closing:** while unsent, the composer's tab shows with its close button, also when it is alone in its group; closing it discards the draft.
- **Main window stays in charge of global composer features:** a chat window's composer never takes the main window's tours, tryouts, onboarding targets, workspace selection or Voice Mode, so opening one doesn't disconnect a running Voice Mode.

Also included, as a separate commit: **Quick input: track modifier keys in windows registered before it.** The quick input tracked Alt/Cmd only in the main window and in windows registered after it was created. It is created on first use, so in a window that already existed, such as a chat window restored after a reload, Alt+Enter or Cmd+Enter in a picker acted as plain Enter. It now also tracks the windows registered before it.

Specs updated: `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md` (draft slots; new sessions in chat windows) and `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS_LIST.md` (a draft slot's custom group).

## Commits

1. Sessions: new-session drafts can be held in independent slots
2. Sessions list: sessions sent from a draft slot join the slot's group
3. Sessions: a new-session composer can keep its drafts for a host outside the main window
4. Sessions: a hosted composer keeps its input in its host's snapshot
5. Sessions: a hosted composer aims for its host's requested target
6. Quick input: track modifier keys in windows registered before it
7. Sessions: a chat window can show a new-session composer as a chat
8. Sessions: chat window composers restore after a reload
9. Sessions: a chat window composer gets back the prompt of a failed background send
10. Sessions: a chat window's unsent composer can't leave its window
11. Sessions: a chat window composer keeps the Dev Container of the session it inherits from
12. Sessions: New Session in a chat window opens a new session there
13. Sessions: a chat window's new sessions don't take the main window's composer actions or tours
14. Sessions: document new sessions in chat windows
15. Sessions list: a slot's send keeps its group while its session drops out of the list
16. Sessions: chat window new-session tests and fixtures pass on every platform and test runner

Commits 15 and 16 address review and CI feedback:

- **Group placement during a provider change (review):** a session sent from a chat window lost its custom group when it briefly dropped out of the sessions list while its request ran, such as while its provider was replaced. It now keeps the group until the request ends.
- **Cmd/Ctrl+N test on Linux and Windows:** the test resolved the running platform's keybindings as macOS. It now checks the keybinding on macOS, Linux and Windows.
- **Browser unit tests:** the new-session widget tests for a chat window composer lacked the agent host filter service that the web code reads, and expected the No Workspace option, which the web doesn't offer.
- **Sessions list Playwright fixtures:** the fixtures' management service didn't provide the request events the sessions groups service now listens to, so the list didn't render.

## How to test

With `sessions.chatWindows.enabled` on, in the Agents window:

1. Open a session in a chat window (sessions list > Open in > New Window).
2. Press Cmd/Ctrl+N in the chat window. A New Session tab opens next to the chat, with its folder, agent, model and mode. Press Cmd/Ctrl+N again: the same composer gets focus.
3. Type a prompt and send. The tab becomes the new session's chat, with an empty input. The main window doesn't change, and the session shows in the same custom group as the source session.
4. Open another composer, type, and reload the window. The composer comes back with its text.
5. With an unsent composer in the window, Move to Main Window is disabled. Running it anyway shows the reason.
6. Open the window's Sessions picker, choose New Session, and press Alt+Enter: the composer opens beside the active chat with its own tab. Its × discards it.
7. Alt+Enter (Send in Background) in a composer starts the session in the background. The composer stays, with "Message sent" and Open Session.
8. Reload with a chat window open, then, before opening any other picker, open its Sessions picker and hold Alt or Cmd while pressing Enter on New Session: the composer opens beside the active chat.

## Validation

At the final tip, rebased on current `main` (counts below were taken before commits 15 and 16; those commits were validated on their own as listed at the end):

- `pnpm run typecheck-client` at each of the 14 commits: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run <test files changed by the commit>` at each commit: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run <file>` at the tip, all passing:

- `./scripts/test.sh --runList <affected folders>`: 6402 passing, 22 pending, 0 failing.
- Each new test was checked to fail with its fix reverted: 101 of 102 mutations fail. The one that survives removes the line that passes the voice eligibility into the composer's options in the `NewChatWidget` constructor; no unit test constructs a full `NewChatWidget`, so that line is verified by reading the source, while the method it calls is tested.
- `pnpm run eslint <changed files>`, `pnpm run valid-layers-check`, `pnpm run check-cyclic-dependencies`: passed. `git diff --check`: clean.
- Performance, measured locally against `main`: no regression. Startup and the main window's New Session are within noise, opening a chat window composer creates no extra chat widgets, 20 composer open and close cycles leak nothing, and typing in a composer writes no storage per keystroke.
- Commits 15 and 16: `pnpm run typecheck-client` at both; Electron `newChatWidget` 246, `chatWindowContribution` 14, `sessionGroupsService` 75 passing; Chromium (`pnpm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium`) the same files and all of `vs/sessions` (7893 passing, 0 failing); the `sessionsListTwistie` Playwright fixture tests, 34 passing; ESLint and layers check passed.
- Manually verified in a Code - OSS dev build:
  - the entry points and their keys, including Alt+Enter and Cmd+Enter in the Sessions picker of a chat window restored after a reload, before any other picker was opened;
  - the inherited defaults;
  - sending in place, and that the input stays empty after a delayed send, a reload and Move to Main Window;
  - restore after a reload;
  - the move refusals and Move to Main Window being disabled;
  - the composer's tab-bar menu and its close button, also alone in a group;
  - the background send.

## Known issues (not addressed here)

- **Test isolation:** `chatWindowChangesetActions.test.ts` fails when loaded together with `agentMergeActions.test.ts` in one test run (a pre-existing upstream issue on main).
- **Browser tabs:** browser tabs opened from a chat window's composer don't follow its draft's network (follow-up).
- **Picker shortcuts:** the new-session pickers' focus shortcuts don't reach a chat window's composer.
- **Cmd+W:** in a chat window, Cmd+W from a chat input closes its group rather than the chat. A chat alone in its group merges into the neighboring group. This also happens on main.
- **Dictate focus:** after Alt+Enter in a composer, focus moves to its Dictate button. The main window's composer does the same.
- **Draft slot lifetime:** a background send that outlives its chat window composer keeps that composer's model in memory until the send ends, through the draft slot's re-adopt check. It never restores into a closed composer.
- **F1:** F1 in a chat window lists both "Agents: New Session" and the main window's "Chat: New Session" with the same key.
- **Not tested manually:**
  - Voice Mode and dictation with a chat window composer, because starting them asks for microphone permission; unit tests cover that the composer never becomes the Voice Mode target;
  - the Dev Container defaults, which are covered by unit tests.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous event path and whole-model/projection calls are explicit. The exact visible delay depends on prompt and reference size, so the magnitude is medium, but the repeated allocation mechanism and scaling are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Full prompt strings plus cloned attachment/reference arrays and projection objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each edit performs work proportional to the current prompt length plus attachment/reference count; typing a prompt from length 0 to N makes the new snapshot work grow quadratically in N, with additional duplicate events possible from inline-reference updates.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Synchronous typing latency and CPU/GC pressure for long or attachment-rich prompts
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Without a host input snapshot, SharedChatInputComposer persisted its full draft only from `saveState`; ordinary model-content changes did not rebuild a complete draft snapshot. Chat-window composers did not previously exist.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new model-content listener synchronously calls `_writeInputSnapshot` for every edit. That method calls `getInputValue`, clones all attachments, and projects/clones draft references before replacing the snapshot.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 750 newly attaches full snapshot reconstruction to every editor model-content event for hosted composers; previously the full draft was written only by `saveState`.
Findings.Title: Coalesce full draft snapshots off the typing path
Findings.Impact: Editing or pasting a long prompt in a chat-window composer repeatedly reconstructs the entire prompt state on the UI input event, which can make continued typing lag and generate avoidable garbage.
Findings.Evidence: RIGHT line 750 registers `write` directly on every `onDidChangeModelContent`. `_writeInputSnapshot` at line 781 reads the complete prompt and clones attachments/references. `ChatWidget.getInput()` delegates to `ChatInputPart.getPromptText()`, whose inline-attachment path projects `model.getValue()` across pills/references; `_getDraftReferences` invokes projection again, so a text edit can traverse/materialize the full model twice before returning.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep edits cheap by marking the snapshot dirty and coalescing reconstruction, then synchronously flush the latest editor state on host save, view handoff/disposal, and send boundaries so reload and failure-recovery semantics remain exact.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The constructor order, separate composer view, and inactive-view retention are directly established in the code. Exact bytes and milliseconds depend on component implementations and how many drafts users keep open, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DOM nodes, context keys, service/listener objects, and UI component instances
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The retained cost grows once per unsent composer tab; inactive view-editor tabs remain alive until their input closes or moves.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher composer-open latency and retained UI memory
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, ChatEditorContent represented an actual chat, so its eagerly constructed ChatGroupView was the visible/required content. There was no composer-only path that constructed a second view while leaving the group unused.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added composer branch runs after the constructor has already created ChatGroupView, then creates a separate NewChatView and replaces the group's DOM element. The hidden group remains owned by ChatEditorContent.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 142 adds a composer-only display state to ChatEditorContent even though the same instance has already eagerly constructed its ChatGroupView; this newly puts that full tree on every unsent-composer path.
Findings.Title: Defer the hidden chat group for composer-only tabs
Findings.Impact: Opening an unsent composer synchronously constructs both the full chat-group shell and the composer view. Each additional unsent tab retains the unused group while hidden, increasing open latency and memory in chat windows with several drafts.
Findings.Evidence: ChatEditorContent eagerly creates ChatGroupView at line 134 before the added `showsComposer` branch at line 142; `_showComposer` then creates a separate view at line 168 and replaces the container child. ChatGroupView's constructor creates a scoped instantiation service/context keys, SessionRemoteConnection, header, composite bar, banner, activity bar, and their DOM/listeners. ViewEditorPane explicitly retains inactive view-editor views in `hiddenViews`, so switching tabs does not release this unused tree.
Findings.Recommendation: Create the ChatGroupView lazily when chat content first becomes available (or dispose/recreate it across the composer-to-chat handoff), so a composer-only tab owns only its NewChatView while preserving the existing focus/model handoff.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and keep one or more unsent new-session composers in a chat window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command resolves the active chat, creates a composer model/slot, opens a view editor, constructs ChatEditorContent, and synchronously builds the visible NewChatView before the composer can be used. The eagerly built ChatGroupView is also on this critical path although it is immediately hidden.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of unsent composer tabs retained across chat-window groups; users can return to a normal chat and open additional composers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One editor-open sequence per command. Different composer opens are user-serialized, and inactive view-editor tabs remain retained rather than disposed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache avoids the duplicated UI construction. Existing chat/provider target data is read locally; each composer gets a fresh slot, input snapshot, ChatGroupView shell, and NewChatView.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor order, component creation, DOM replacement, and hidden-view retention are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact construction time and retained bytes depend on the contributed group components and number of drafts users keep open.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression: every composer-only editor constructs and retains a full unused chat-group UI tree in addition to its required composer view.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type, attach context, and persist an unsent chat-window composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every model-content event synchronously reconstructs the host snapshot before the input event returns. Actual storage serialization occurs only during the workbench storage save event, not per keystroke.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store the marshalled array of live and unrestored chat-window composers in workspace machine storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One storage operation per storage save event, containing all currently live and retained stored composers
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Chat-window composers and their persisted snapshots did not exist; the main composer stored its own draft through its existing saveState path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the ordinary typing path; it runs on save/shutdown and must complete as part of state persistence.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Current prompt length, attachment/reference count, number of edits, and number of live/stored composers serialized at save time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Input handlers run synchronously and sequentially on the UI thread. Storage saves serialize all composer snapshots in one save callback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The in-memory snapshot always replaces the prior full state; there is no dirty-bit, debounce, incremental representation, or coalescing. A stored snapshot is parsed once on restore.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the edit listener, full prompt read, duplicate inline projection, and array cloning are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical prompts are small, but long pasted/generated prompts and inline references make the per-edit full-model projection and allocation materially larger.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable serialization/allocation regression: full draft reconstruction is newly placed on every text edit rather than coalesced or flushed at lifecycle boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send a chat-window composer in the foreground
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workspace validation, provider preparation/configuration, chat creation, and provider request dispatch must complete before the tab transitions to the created session. Composer/model handoff and request ownership tracking remain active until request end.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider preparation/config lookup, createNewChat, and sendRequest for the new session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider chain per accepted foreground send
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider operations existed for the main-window composer, but a chat-window composer could not previously place this chain on its own tab path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the foreground-send critical path; the tab cannot become the final created-session chat until it completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One provider request chain per foreground send; prompt and attached-context payload size controls serialization/network cost.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A foreground send is sequential within the composer. Session replacement listeners follow one request and dispose at request end.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider/session caches remain authoritative and unchanged. ChatModelHold prevents a duplicate model load during the composer-to-chat handoff and releases after binding.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for path and cardinality; provider-specific transport cost is variable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider implementations may use local IPC, subprocesses, or remote network calls with widely varying duration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance finding: the new scenario intentionally invokes one existing provider chain per send, with no diff-added fan-out or duplicate load.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send repeatedly in the background from a chat-window composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The initial validation and scheduling/reseed must complete before the composer is ready for another prompt; remote provider completion and failure recovery continue off the composer's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Asynchronous provider preparation and request dispatch for each background session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider chain per explicit background send; aggregate concurrency equals user-started in-flight sends
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Background provider chains already existed for the main-window composer; chat-window composers could not initiate them before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completion is off the composer critical path after scheduling, though draft reseeding remains on the immediate interaction path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of user-triggered background sends still in flight; each retains one bounded tracking store and one provider request until completion.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Multiple background sends can overlap by design with no shared limiter. Each send has independent listeners and cleanup at request end; this behavior already exists for the main composer and is newly exposed in chat windows.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache applies. Each send creates a new draft/session; tracking is removed on success, failure, cancellation, or rejected dispatch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for concurrency and cleanup mechanics.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual overlap depends on user send rate and provider duration; no evidence shows realistic uncontrolled automatic bursts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: concurrency is explicit per user send, tracking is bounded to in-flight work, and cleanup follows request completion.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore chat windows, their tabs, and unsent composers after reload
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After initial session restore, stored windows are processed sequentially; each restorable chat is checked and its auxiliary window/editor tabs are opened in stored order. Stored composer attempts may wait briefly for their session to become known.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and later rewrite stored chat-window/composer state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per restoration service construction and one write per storage save event
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Chat-window state was already read and written; the diff extends its contents and retention rules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read gates knowing what to restore; writes occur on state-save events.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/reveal auxiliary windows and open restored editor tabs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one window open per stored window entry and one chat resolution/editor open per restorable chat
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: New windows already restored their chats serially; when a root chat resolved to an existing window, the sibling chats were previously skipped rather than restored there.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each stored window's tabs are awaited in order before that restoration entry completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for provider/session restoration and resolve whether stored chats still exist
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One check per stored chat after session restore, with local resolution first and a bounded wait when not yet known
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Stored chat-window restoration already checked canRestore for each candidate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A chat must be deemed restorable before its window/tab can open.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of stored chat windows plus chats/tabs in each window; failed stored entries are retried once on a later startup until opened or removed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Stored windows and chats within a window are restored serially to preserve tab/group order. Opens of unrelated chats are otherwise sequenced by chat key in ChatWindowService.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Storage is parsed once. Known canonical chat mappings avoid retaining aliases after restore. Failed entries remain as a bounded stored set and are retired when their chat opens or is removed; there is no retry within one startup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for serial cardinality and lifecycle bounds; no evidence establishes a new unbounded or duplicated boundary burst.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical stored window/tab counts are small; provider loading and auxiliary-window creation duration varies. Permanently failed opens now retry on later startups, but only once per retained entry per startup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression beyond the submitted findings: the new reveal path performs the missing required tab restores with the same ordering constraints, and retained failures are bounded and retired on open/removal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create Quick Input after auxiliary chat windows already exist
Scenarios.CriticalPath: QuickInputController construction enumerates registered windows once and registers modifier-key listeners before the picker is used.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of currently registered auxiliary windows, normally a small user-bounded set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous one-time loop; later windows continue through the existing registration event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The registered window list is read once at construction. Listener disposables are owned by each window and released on unregister.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Window count varies, but each entry adds only bounded DOM event listeners.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: one-time O(window count) listener registration is bounded and correctly tied to window disposal.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 58 changed files and relevant production/test hunks. Submitted two medium-confidence-impact, high-mechanism-confidence findings: eager retention of an unused ChatGroupView for every composer-only tab, and synchronous whole-draft reconstruction on every editor change. Traced provider, storage, auxiliary-window, restoration, concurrency, cache, and cleanup behavior for all important touched scenarios; no additional high-confidence boundary, cache, or lifecycle regression met the reporting bar.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
